A nearly linear randomized filter for pairwise mixing

Let P be a table of N=2nN=2^n images, with n≥1n\ge1, and fix an error budget 0<ε<10<\varepsilon<1. There is an algorithm with the following guarantees for each fixed input table, over the algorithm's independent random choices.

  • Every table reported as mixing really mixes.
  • A mixing table is reported as mixing with probability at least 1−ε1-\varepsilon.
  • The worst-case cost is O(Nn4log(Nn/ε))O(N n^4\log(Nn/\varepsilon)) word operations and O(N)O(N) working words. The Python implementation batches the probability checks using O(n+log(1/ε))O(n+\log(1/\varepsilon))-bit integers. Repeating them with single-bit weights gives the same time bound with O(n)O(n)-bit transform arithmetic, as shown below.

One can interpret the other answer as unresolved, use it as a one-sided Monte Carlo prediction of nonmixing, or run the deterministic classifier on the unresolved inputs for an exact decision. In the last mode the worst-case fallback still takes quadratic time. The guarantee addresses classification and places no bound on the mixing time.

For an exact answer on a fixed mixing table, set ε≤1/N\varepsilon\le 1/N and enable the deterministic fallback. Its expected contribution is then at most εO(N2)=O(N)\varepsilon\,O(N^2)=O(N), so the overall expected time is nearly linear on every mixer. Nonmixers always reach the fallback and can still require quadratic time.

What suffices to certify mixing

An ordered pair of table inputs (x,y)(x,y) gives a directed edge

a=x⊕y→b=P(x)⊕P(y).a=x\oplus y \ \longrightarrow\ b=P(x)\oplus P(y).

The vertices of interest are the N−1N-1 nonzero differences. Pairs with x=yx=y give the auxiliary edge 0→00\to0 and can be ignored. The chain is an average of permutations, so weak connectivity implies strong connectivity, and the uniform law on differences is stationary. To certify mixing, we can exhibit a spanning tree of real edges with directions retained, then prove that the full graph has period one. One bit is immediate because its graph has just one vertex. Difference-chain proof

First, the implementation samples up to three inputs xx and searches just the edges supplied by those inputs. Each fixed xx permutes the differences. If the sampled support is already connected and aperiodic, all its connecting paths and cycles are still present in the full graph, which therefore mixes. Otherwise its edges seed the forest. This initial test costs O(N)O(N) time.

Finding a crossing edge for many components at once

Signed sums for recovering crossing edges also appear in graph sketching. Here the two ends of each edge are XOR differences, which lets the table produce all the signed sums through convolutions. Ahn, Guha and McGregor, Analyzing Graph Structure via Linear Measurements

Maintain a forest. A crossing pair for a tree component SS is a pair (x,y)(x,y) whose edge has exactly one endpoint in SS. Given two subsets X,YX,Y of the table inputs, consider all ordered pairs in the rectangle X×YX\times Y. For each component SS, compute three signed sums over these pairs, using the weights w(x,y)=1,x,yw(x,y)=1,x,y respectively. The summand is

w(x,y)(𝟏S(x⊕y)−𝟏S(P(x)⊕P(y))).w(x,y)\bigl(\mathbf1_S(x\oplus y)-\mathbf1_S(P(x)\oplus P(y))\bigr).

Pairs internal or external to SS cancel individually. If precisely one pair crosses the cut, the three results are s,sx,sys,sx,sy for a sign s∈{−1,1}s\in\{-1,1\}. Whenever the first value is ±1\pm1, recover the candidate x,yx,y by division. Check that both are in range and use the table to check that their edge crosses the cut. A collision of several pairs can also suggest a candidate, but this last check ensures that only genuine crossing edges enter the forest.

The three signed sums are computable for all components together in O(Nn)O(Nn) time. For an XOR convolution write

(A*B)(a)=∑xA(x)B(x⊕a).(A*B)(a)=\sum_x A(x)B(x\oplus a).

With A=𝟏XA=\mathbf1_X and B=𝟏YB=\mathbf1_Y, one convolution counts all pairs in the rectangle by input difference. Replacing each input array UU by U∘P−1U\circ P^{-1} gives the counts by output difference. Subtract these two arrays and aggregate their entries by component. For the endpoint moments, repeat after multiplying the relevant input array by its input index, before reordering. A fast Walsh–Hadamard transform computes each convolution in O(Nn)O(Nn) additions, subtractions and multiplications. Indeed each Walsh character χu(x)=(−1)u⋅x\chi_u(x)=(-1)^{u\cdot x} satisfies χu(x⊕y)=χu(x)χu(y)\chi_u(x\oplus y)=\chi_u(x)\chi_u(y), so the transform of a convolution is the coordinatewise product of the transforms. Applying the same transform again and dividing by NN recovers the convolution. Each of the nn bit positions contributes one stage of N/2N/2 independent sum-and-difference operations. The integer intermediates for these cut sums are polynomially bounded in NN, so O(n)O(n)-bit words suffice.

Why the sampled rectangles find even a rare edge

A pass tries inclusion probabilities 2−i,2−j2^{-i},2^{-j} for 0≤i,j≤n0\le i,j\le n. At level ii, include each first input independently in XX with probability 2−i2^{-i}. Keep this XX while trying all second-input levels jj. For each jj, sample YY independently of XX, including each second input with probability 2−j2^{-j}. The rectangles can be processed one at a time.

Fix a component with at least one crossing pair. Let kk be the number of first inputs xx that occur in such a pair. Some level gives a probability pp in [1/(2k),1/k][1/(2k),1/k]. Exactly one of these kk inputs is selected with probability kp(1−p)k−1≥1/4kp(1-p)^{k-1}\ge1/4. Indeed this expression increases up to p=1/kp=1/k, and at p=1/(2k)p=1/(2k) Bernoulli's inequality gives the bound. Conditioned on the unique selected first input, apply the same argument to its number of crossing second inputs. The appropriate second level selects exactly one of them with probability at least 1/41/4. Thus one pass discovers a genuine crossing edge for this component with probability at least 1/161/16, regardless of how sparse the cut is.

Freeze the component labels at the start of each phase. Run independent passes to find one outgoing undirected edge per component that has one. Merge along these edges, retaining the directed witnesses when joining distinct components. On a connected graph, a phase finding an edge for every component at least halves the component count when it exceeds one. After at most nn such phases the forest spans the full graph. In a disconnected graph the same argument applies inside each true component. It is enough to stop a phase as soon as its component count has halved. It is also safe to return unresolved if a phase exhausts its budget before the count halves. An implementation can warm-start with any verified edges. Each success is still backed by actual directed edges. A premature stop can send a mixer to the unresolved set.

There are at most NnNn cut tests over the phases. Conditional on all previous phases, the chance to miss a specified nonempty cut in rr fresh passes is at most (15/16)r(15/16)^r. A union bound applies even though earlier phases and their edges determine the later cuts.

Certifying the period without enumerating the remaining edges

Take the spanning tree and assign integer heights hh. Give its root height zero, add one when traversing a tree edge in its recorded direction, and subtract one in the other direction. For any directed graph edge a→ba\to b put z(a,b)=h(a)+1−h(b)z(a,b)=h(a)+1-h(b). The period dd is exactly the gcd of the |z(a,b)||z(a,b)|. To see this, the signed expressions sum to the length around every directed cycle. Conversely, directed distances from the root are well defined modulo dd because two directed paths to a vertex can be closed with the same return path. Every edge advances this residue by one. The tree heights obey these same congruences, so dd divides every z(a,b)z(a,b).

Each of the dd cyclic classes has equal stationary mass because every step passes its mass to the next class. The stationary law is uniform, so dd divides N−1N-1. Initialize g=N−1g=N-1. Each time a real edge has g∤z(a,b)g\nmid z(a,b), replace gg by gcd(g,|z(a,b)|)\gcd(g,|z(a,b)|). The true period still divides gg. Reaching g=1g=1 on a connected graph certifies mixing. Every strict update at least halves gg. A disjoint-set forest that tracks relative heights can maintain this gcd while edges are inserted. Joining two components adds a constant to the heights in one tree, preserving all previous within-tree discrepancies. An edge within a tree supplies a discrepancy immediately.

For g>1g>1, define A(a)=(h(a)+1)modgA(a)=(h(a)+1)\bmod g and B(b)=h(b)modgB(b)=h(b)\bmod g on the nonzero differences. Set A(0)=B(0)=0A(0)=B(0)=0. A random probe independently draws a fair bit r(y)r(y) for each table input and computes all fingerprints

E(x)=∑yr(y)(A(x⊕y)−B(P(x)⊕P(y))).E(x)=\sum_y r(y)\bigl(A(x\oplus y)-B(P(x)\oplus P(y))\bigr).

These are again two XOR convolutions, the second using r∘P−1r\circ P^{-1} and then evaluating the result at P(x)P(x). If E(x)≠0E(x)\ne0, scan that row to find an actual violated congruence and update gg. If any edge violates the congruence, select one such (x,y)(x,y) for the proof. Conditional on all other bits, at most one value of r(y)r(y) can make E(x)E(x) zero because its coefficient is nonzero. Thus a probe detects some violation with probability at least 1/21/2. More generally, drawing each coordinate independently and uniformly from {0,…,2b−1}\{0,\ldots,2^b-1\} gives miss probability at most 2−b2^{-b}. If the candidate is valid, every probe is identically zero.

The same fingerprint accelerates connectivity. For a proposed partition, take A(a)=B(a)A(a)=B(a) equal to the integer label of its component and set A(0)=B(0)=0A(0)=B(0)=0. A nonzero row exposes a real edge between two components. One can add every directed edge at the exposed first input xx by scanning the NN second inputs. If all fingerprints vanish while more than one component remains, returning unresolved costs at most 2−b2^{-b} in false-exclusion probability on a connected graph. The cyclic-color probe likewise permits adding a whole exposed row.

Algorithm and error budget

start with isolated differences and add verified edges at sampled first inputs
for up to n phases, while multiple components remain:
    optionally try a partition fingerprint, adding a whole row if it exposes one
    use independent rectangle passes with frozen component labels as needed
    after the first full pass, optionally probe the current partition again
    merge verified crossing edges until the count at label-freeze time has halved
    if the phase exhausts its budget first, return unresolved
if the forest does not span all differences, return unresolved
take g from the forest, initialized to N - 1 and updated with witnessed edges
while g exceeds one:
    test the cyclic colors for g with an independent fingerprint
    if no violation was found, return unresolved
    add the exposed row, updating g from its real edges
return certified mixing

For an error target ε=2−e\varepsilon=2^{-e}, a conservative pass limit per phase is r=16(e+n+⌈log2(n+1)⌉+2)r=16(e+n+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil+2). Since (15/16)r≤exp(−r/16)≤2−r/16(15/16)^r\le \exp(-r/16)\le 2^{-r/16}, the NnNn cut tests together cost at most ε/4\varepsilon/4 in false-exclusion probability. For each partition or cyclic-color fingerprint take b=e+⌈log2(3n+4)⌉+1b=e+\lceil\log_2(3n+4)\rceil+1. There are at most 2n2n phase partition checks and at most n+1n+1 period checks. With fresh coordinates at each check their combined miss bound is at most ε/2\varepsilon/2, including room for preliminary checks. Thus the chance that a mixing input is unresolved is at most ε\varepsilon. The implementation uses integer bit lengths, which can round these limits up by one at powers of two. Scanning sparse rectangles with at most NN pairs recovers every edge in that rectangle within O(Nn)O(Nn) time including disjoint-set updates. Any smaller work budget still preserves the guarantee that every reported mixer is genuine, with the false-exclusion bound adjusted to that budget.

There are at most nn phases of (n+1)2(n+1)^2 rectangles per pass, each costing O(Nn)O(Nn) word operations. Batched fingerprints use O(n+e)O(n+e)-bit integers. Equivalently one can take bb independent fair-bit probes per check to retain the O(n)O(n)-bit arithmetic bound. Even with these repeated probes the period stage costs only O(Nn2log(Nn/ε))O(Nn^2\log(Nn/\varepsilon)) word operations. Streaming transforms and retaining only a forest and component labels uses O(N)O(N) words. The polynomial in n=log2Nn=\log_2 N and the constants matter for small tables. Verified sparse edges can finish the decision before the first expensive rectangle pass. The bounds use independent random bits.
